title: Rhombus Retail integration prospect diary
content:
2026-03-10 — quick dump / working diary

Context: Rhombus Retail (mid-market omnichannel retailer, ~120 stores, headless commerce backend, shopper loyalty app). Heard via conference intro (RetailNow Q4) that they're experimenting with automated product description generation and a chat assistant for store associates. Possible fit: Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput during end-of-season pushes + Private deployment for PII rules on loyalty data.

High-level account notes
- HQ: Austin, TX. Engineering org ~18, product ~12. CTO: Lina Park. Head of ML/AI: Marcus Reed (VP Product ML).
- Current stack: Headless commerce (CommerceCore), Postgres for orders, Redis cache, proprietary mobile app. They use AWS across accounts.
- Pain signals: slow copy ops for merchandising (manual descriptions), store agents switching to consumer app for answers (latency/accuracy issues), cost surprise on current vendor during holiday spikes.
- Security: strict PII redaction requirements, need to keep loyalty identifiers in-house. They asked about KMS/HSM and VPC peering in a prior call (see notes).
- Buying motion: likely product-led pilot -> pilot -> dedicated contract. Typical procurement timeline 3-6 months. Budget sensitivity until Q3.

Decision makers / Influencers (from LinkedIn + intro)
- Marcus Reed (VP Product ML) — primary technical champion. cares about latency and model control.
- Lina Park (CTO) — cares about org risk, vendor SLAs, private deployments.
- Denise Carter (Director Merchandising) — product owner for content pipelines. Interested in time-savings for merchandising team.
- Ben O'Neil (Platform Eng lead) — will own integration (KMS, VPC, SSO).

Initial hypothesis: run a 6-week pilot scoped to: product description generation + in-store Q&A assistant. Use Redwood Private (VPC) for pilot with small dedicated capacity. Evaluate: latency (95th < 200ms for short responses), quality metric (human-rated pass rate > 88%), cost per 1k tokens.

Technical constraints to validate (todo items)
- Confirm VPC peering policy and if on-prem option needed. (ask Ben)
- Does their legal require per-request audit logs retained 7 years? (ask Lina)
- Which identity provider (Okta?) for SSO and SCIM? (ask Ben)
- Existing inference provider? (we need logs for cost comparison)

Outbound plan (sequence draft)
1) Short intro email — subject: "Rhombus + Redwood — reduce merch copy time by 80%". 2) Follow-up: one-pager + short case study (retail) + proposal for 6-week pilot. 3) If no response: 2 LinkedIn InMails spread 7 days apart. 4) Warm intro ask via mutual connection from RetailNow (if available). 5) Call to action: 30 min pilot scoping call.

Seed email (working)
Subject: Rhombus + Redwood — 6-week pilot to automate product copy + in-store answers
Hi Marcus / Denise,

Quick note — enjoyed your talk at RetailNow. I think there’s a simple pilot that could save your merch team hours per product and cut support load for store associates. Redwood runs a private inference stack that lets you keep loyalty identifiers in your VPC while we run optimized LLMs with predictable latency and cost.

Proposal: 6-week pilot (scope: automated product description batch generator + in-store QA assistant integration). We’ll handle: model selection, latency SLO tuning, a small dedicated pool for peak periods, and integration guidance for Okta + KMS.

Can we book 30 minutes next week to sketch scope? Happy to share an anonymized ROI example from a comparable retailer.

— Avery

Call agenda (30 min scoping)
- 5m intros
- 5m high-level goals and success criteria (Denise / merchandising)
- 5m tech constraints (Ben)
- 7m pilot plan + timeline + what we need from Rhombus (sample SKUs, test users)
- 5m commercial framing (est. cost ballpark, pilot included)
- 3m next steps

Objection handling (quick bullets)
- "We already use Vendor X and switching is risky": ask which parts are painful today — cost or latency? Offer A/B pilot vs baseline and fallbacks.
- "We can’t expose loyalty IDs": confirm Private/VPC option + KMS. Offer tokenization pattern and redaction pipeline example.
- "It’s too expensive": propose a limited scope pilot, show batch vs real-time tradeoffs and quality-cost tuning, recommend quantized model variant for cost savings.
- "We don’t have infra bandwidth": offer Redwood-managed setup for pilot, 1-2 weeks runbook and an SRE touchpoint.

Competitive landscape / notes
- Vendor X: current incumbent (T&S) — charges per inference; struggles on holiday spikes and has slower kernel-level optimizations.
- Vendor Y: open-source stack run internally at some teams — good cost but poor ops maturity.
- Our edge: predictable dedicated capacity, private deployment option, built-in caching and automatic prefix caching for catalog prompts. Emphasize measurable unit-cost improvements from Optimize toolkit.

Metrics to collect during pilot
- Latency p95 and p99 for product description generation and chat queries
- Tokens per request average, cost per 1k tokens
- Human quality score (sample of 200 outputs rated by merchandising team)
- Time saved (hrs/week) in the merchandising workflow

Next steps (internal)
- Diego: run a short ROI calc using a sample of 5k SKUs — estimate time saved and projected annualized cost. (owner: Diego, due: 2026-03-15)
- Priya: draft tailored one-pager and anonymized case study for Rhombus (owner: Priya, due: 2026-03-13)
- Me (Avery): warm intro search — find potential mutual connections from RetailNow attendees, reach out on LinkedIn (due: 2026-03-12).

Notes to self (voice memo style)
- Use "pilot:rhombus-2026" as ephemeral internal tag to track artifacts.
- Keep the initial ask light — focus on time-savings and security.
- If Marcus pushes for on-prem, scope a phased approach: Private (VPC) first, option to air-gap later.

Meeting snippets / prior call (2026-03-09)
- Marcus: "we need predictable latency in stores — anything over 300ms means agents swap apps"
- Denise: "our merch team spends an average of 6 hours/week per product on copy"
- Ben: "Okta + AWS KMS, but procurement will want an architecture diagram and audit log retention details"

Questions for next call
- Marcus: acceptable latency SLOs for in-store assistant? p95 and p99 thresholds?
- Denise: sample SLA for quality — will merchandising sign off on 200 samples?
- Ben: who will own network provisioning for a VPC peer? procurement or platform?

End of diary entry.

-- Avery
